selectedIdea.title: The GPS change users did not have to install

synthesis.content:
### Central insight

Contrast ending the use of an existing feature with specifying that a future generation would omit the feature. Build the story around two interventions in the same system.

### Evidence

Selective Availability deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. In May 2000 the US government stopped using it at President Bill Clinton’s direction to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide. In September 2007 the government announced it would procure the future GPS III generation without the feature. GPS.gov describes the procurement choice as making the 2000 policy durable by removing that feature in the future generation.

### What the narrative should emphasize

Contrast ending the use of an existing feature with specifying that a future generation would omit the feature. Build the story around two interventions in the same system.

### Gaps and uncertainty

The 2007 procurement decision was not the 2000 operational switch. Do not infer a date when every satellite lacked the capability, perfect accuracy or a universal quantified benefit.

narrative.content:
### Selected Story
Explain how the US government addressed Selective Availability in two distinct ways: in May 2000, it stopped using the feature that deliberately degraded public GPS signals; in September 2007, it announced that the future GPS III generation would be procured without it. The reader should understand that the first was an operational change and the second a procurement choice intended to make the 2000 policy durable—not one single event.

### Story Progression
- **Context:** Selective Availability deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. In May 2000, the US government stopped using it at President Bill Clinton’s direction to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide.
- **Development:** In September 2007, the government announced it would procure the future GPS III generation without Selective Availability, extending the earlier policy through the design of a future generation.
- **Endpoint:** The story’s central distinction is between ending use of an existing feature and specifying that a future generation omit it: related interventions in the same system, but not the same event.

### Critical Constraints
- Do not imply the 2007 procurement announcement was the 2000 operational switch or give a date when every satellite lacked the feature.
- Do not claim perfect accuracy or a universal, quantified benefit.
- Do not claim users did or did not need to install anything; the supplied material does not establish that.
